facts.text: Unionport’s name comes from the 19th‑century Unionport Company, which aimed to unite scattered Bronx settlements with a ferry and road network along Westchester Creek.
The neighborhood sits between Westchester Avenue, Westchester Creek, Lafayette Avenue, and White Plains Road, forming a compact, historically layered section of the southeastern Bronx.
Unionport’s streets are lined with brick rowhouses, two‑family homes, postwar apartments, and corner storefronts that echo its transition from rural farms to an urban suburb.
Westchester Creek, a tidal inlet that once hosted docks and shipyards, defines Unionport’s geography and once linked the Bronx to Long Island Sound.
The 6 train stops just west of Unionport, and the nearby Parkchester Station offers direct access to Manhattan for commuters and visitors alike.
Unionport’s history includes a 19th‑century ferry service that connected the area to the East River, marketed as a convenient residential hub “within sight of the Sound.”.
